chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Dhubyan ibn Hakim al-Azdi, from Musa ibn Uqayl al-Numayri, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "When two men come to you for a dispute, do not render a verdict for the first one until you have heard from the second one, for if you do that, the judgment will become clear to you."

key_terms.تَقَاضَى: to claim against each other / to come for dispute

ai.seo_question: What is the proper procedure for a judge when hearing a dispute between two parties?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes the principle of *istima’ al-janibayn* (listening to both sides) as a prerequisite for judicial clarity (*tabayyun*). It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on procedural justice, ensuring that a judge does not prematurely favor the first claimant before the full context of the dispute is revealed, thereby preventing hasty or biased rulings.
